content:
Here’s a concise summary:

When analyzing algorithms, runtime depends on input size (e.g., sorting 6 elements vs. 6 billion). Instead of fixed times, we express runtime as a function of input size to understand scalability. We focus on **upper bounds** (worst-case guarantees) because they provide practical assurances to users (e.g., "this won’t take more than 3 seconds"). Lower bounds (e.g., "it takes *at least* 3 seconds") are less useful since they don’t cap runtime. Upper bounds ensure reliability, especially in time-sensitive applications.
